negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf press release, case study or customer reference naming a Kosovo bank was found, despite Kosovo estates plausibly containing legacy Wincor Nixdorf hardware.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only generic global cash-recycling and DN Series portfolio content; no Kosovo mention.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The largest OEM in the region publishes nothing Kosovo-specific, so installed-base evidence for Kosovo must come from the integrator layer (Printec, Payten) or from the banks themselves, not from OEM newsrooms.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found that Euronet or any other independent ATM deployer (IAD) operates a non-bank ATM network in Kosovo.
negative_findings.result_summary: Euronet IAD expansion releases enumerate many European markets (Iceland, Baltics, Norway, Montenegro, Spain, Italy, Belgium) but Kosovo did not appear in any release surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests Kosovo's ATM estate is essentially entirely bank-owned, which means CBK ATM counts and bank disclosures should reconcile without an IAD residual — a useful structural assumption to state and to monitor for change.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language searching for Kosovo ATM/POS vendor and contract terms produced no Kosovo-relevant vendor sources.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cyrillic queries (банкомат, добављач, терминали, платни систем + Kosovo) returned only Serbian and North Macedonian bank general-conditions and internet-banking pages; nothing about Kosovo terminal supply.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor communications aimed at Kosovo appear to be published in Albanian and English only; Serbian-language vendor discovery for this cell has near-zero yield and should be deprioritised in favour of sq/en, except possibly for banks serving Serb-majority municipalities.

negative_findings.description: No public tender award or contract notice naming an ATM/POS supplier to a Kosovo commercial bank was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Tender-aggregator results (globaltenders, tendersinfo) surfaced but contained no accessible Kosovo bank ATM/POS award; commercial banks in Kosovo are private and not subject to public procurement publication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that procurement transparency is not a viable route to vendor-bank linkage for commercial banks here; only CBK's own procurement and vendor self-disclosure remain. Sets expectations for this cell's collection design.

negative_findings.description: Printec Group corporate site returned HTTP 403 and Asseco SEE contacts page returned a redirect loop to automated fetching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are almost certainly live and bot-defended/consent-gated rather than dead; content was corroborated via search snippets and third-party indexes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of the highest-value vendor sources for this cell need a browser-based collector rather than a plain HTTP fetcher; a naive pipeline would wrongly mark them dead.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo customer reference found for the major switch/card-management vendors BPC (SmartVista), OpenWay (Way4), Nexi/SIA, or Tietoevry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multi-vendor searches returned only non-Kosovo case studies; the only confirmed Kosovo card-platform evidence is Compass Plus TranzWare at Quipu's Kosovo processing centre.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Kosovo issuing/acquiring platform landscape is largely undocumented publicly; TranzWare/Quipu is the single confirmed anchor and should be treated as the starting node for snowballing rather than assuming regional-vendor defaults.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language vendor terminology for this cell is thin and partly borrowed from English ('POS', 'terminale', 'bankomat'), and no Albanian-language vendor press room was found — Kosovo integrators appear to publish mostly in English or on LinkedIn.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and test an expanded sq glossary (bankomat, ATM, terminale POS, pajisje fiskale, furnizues i autorizuar, zgjidhje pagesash, personalizim kartelash, rrjeti i bankomatëve, instalim, mirëmbajtje) against Kosovo news portals and LinkedIn Kosovo company posts rather than vendor websites.

coverage_gaps.description: The local reseller/service layer that physically installs and maintains ATM/POS estates in Kosovo is not yet enumerated; only CACTTUS and the ASEE/Payten and Printec regional entities were identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scrape the STIKK member directory and KIESA sector listings, cross-join with the ARBK business registry on NACE codes for computer/hardware services, and check each candidate's site for bank references.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor deployment announcements for this market increasingly appear on LinkedIn company pages rather than corporate newsrooms (the one confirmed Kosovo Printec win surfaced on Facebook, not the website).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish a compliant social-monitoring routine (LinkedIn company page follows, saved searches) for Printec, Payten/ASEE, Cacttus, Quipu and Kosovo bank pages; avoid ToS-violating scraping.

coverage_gaps.description: The strongest Kosovo vendor evidence found is from 2016 (Quipu/Compass Plus contactless) and an undated Printec/BPB post; there is little recent (2023-2026) vendor-side quantification of Kosovo deployments.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add archive-based collection (Wayback Machine snapshots of vendor newsrooms and Kosovo bank ATM/branch pages) to reconstruct the deployment timeline, and set forward-looking alerts for new announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-management suppliers (CIT companies, cash-centre automation, note sorters such as Giesecke+Devrient or Glory) serving Kosovo were not covered in this pass, though they are directly relevant to cash-usage intelligence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on cash-in-transit and cash-centre vendors plus CBK cash-processing suppliers, in sq ('transport i vlerave', 'para të gatshme', 'makina numëruese') and en.

brief: Kosovo's ATM/POS and card-infrastructure vendor landscape is documented almost entirely by regional integrators rather than global OEMs: Printec (ATM fleet renewal for BPB Bank), the Asseco SEE/Payten group (registered Kosovo entity in Prishtina, regional POS/ATM managed services), Halcom (Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo digital channel), and Compass Plus, whose TranzWare platform underpins Quipu's Kosovo card processing and personalisation centre — the single richest quantified Kosovo reference found, with dated contactless issuance volumes. Global OEMs (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos) and the major switch vendors (BPC, OpenWay, Nexi, Tietoevry) publish nothing Kosovo-specific, and no independent ATM deployer appears to operate in the market, implying a wholly bank-owned ATM estate. Local-language discovery is asymmetric: Albanian terms surface the fiscal-device/merchant-terminal supplier layer (ATK's authorised-supplier register, STIKK/KIESA directories, CACTTUS), while Serbian-language searching yielded nothing Kosovo-relevant for this cell. Collection should be browser-based (Printec and ASEE both bot-defended or consent-gated to plain fetchers) and should pair vendor newsrooms with Kosovo bank product pages and the Electronic Payments International Kosovo tag as a pre-filtered tripwire.
